chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa from al-'Abbas ibn Ma'ruf from 'Ali ibn Mahziyar, who said:

I read in the book of 'Abdullah ibn Muhammad to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), 'May I be your ransom,' that it was narrated from Abu 'Abdullah (peace be upon him) that he said: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) designated zakat upon nine items: upon wheat, barley, dates, raisins, gold, silver, sheep, cattle, and camels, and the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) pardoned/exempted what is besides that.'

The questioner said to him: 'We have many things that are multiples of that.' He said to him, 'What is it?' He said to him, 'Rice.' So Abu 'Abdullah (peace be upon him) said to him, 'I say to you that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) designated the charity (zakat) upon nine items and pardoned what is besides that, and you say that we have rice and we have sorghum/durra? Sorghum was present during the time of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family).'
So he (peace be upon him) wrote: 'Thus it is, and zakat is upon all that which is measured by the sa'.'

If it were not that he (peace be upon him) meant by his statement 'and zakat is upon all that which is measured by the sa'' what we have previously mentioned of recommendation and preference, he would not have validated the statement of the questioner that zakat is upon nine items and that what is besides it is exempted, and that Abu 'Abdullah (peace be upon him) objected to the one who said 'we have rice and sorghum,' admonishing him that there is no obligatory zakat in it. And his statement 'thus it is' along with his statement 'and zakat is upon all that which is measured by the sa'' would be contradictory, and this is not permissible in their statements (peace be upon them). And what indicates what we mentioned is also what he narrated:

key_terms.الصَّاعُ: A traditional unit of volume measurement

ai.seo_question: What are the nine items upon which zakat is obligatory according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* delineates the nine specific categories of obligatory zakat, distinguishing them from other commodities like rice and sorghum which were not subject to mandatory dues in the Prophet's time. The Imam’s clarification that 'zakat is in everything measured by the sa' refers to recommended (mustahabb) rather than obligatory (wajib) dues, resolving the apparent contradiction with his rejection of rice as a mandatory category. This distinction highlights the Shia scholarly approach to differentiating between fixed scriptural obligations and broader principles of charity.
